transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, uh... I’m here because things at work have gotten strange since I got that county safety award. I’m a transportation inspector, so reports are kind of my whole job, and now certain people are twisting what I write, asking these pointed budget questions like they’re trying to make me look crooked.

My supervisor keeps saying it’s just normal review, but it doesn’t feel normal. It’s coordinated, you know? Like they’re trying to discredit me. And it’s funny, because before that award nobody cared this much about my reports—well, except when the bridge detour thing happened, but that was a whole mess with scheduling and the county office never reads emails properly anyway. But this is different. I can tell they’re setting something up.
Do you feel that people are picking on you, trying to harm you, or that certain events or actions are specifically targeted at you?

Yeah, yes—targeted is the word I’d use. Ever since that county safety award, certain people at work have been… I don’t know, twisting my inspection reports, picking at little things, asking these pointed budget questions like they’re trying to make me look crooked.

My supervisor keeps telling me it’s just normal review, but I’ve done this job long enough to know what normal review looks like. This feels coordinated. Like they’re trying to discredit me. And it’s not like I’m careless with reports—I mean, I keep copies, I label things, I even have this whole folder system because back in high school my shop teacher was big on documentation, and that stuck with me—but now suddenly everyone’s acting like my paperwork is suspicious. So yeah, I do feel like it’s aimed at me.
Do you ever feel that things people say or do in public, like on TV or in conversations, are directed at you or have a special meaning for you personally?

Not like TV, no… I don’t sit there thinking the news anchor is talking to me or anything. It’s more at work. Like, since I got that county safety award, people started acting different around my inspection reports.

They’ll say things in meetings—little comments about budgets or “clarifying documentation”—and it sounds general, but I know it’s aimed at me. They’re twisting what I wrote, making it look like I’m doing something wrong. My supervisor says it’s just normal review, but I’ve been doing this long enough to know the difference. It feels coordinated, like they’re trying to discredit me.

And I keep thinking, if nobody had made such a big deal about that award, maybe this wouldn’t have started. Awards are funny like that—my cousin got one once for volunteer firefighting and suddenly everyone wanted to argue about who deserved what. People get weird when somebody gets recognized.
Outside of work, have you ever felt that things people say or do—like in public places, on the radio, or online—have a special meaning for you or are directed at you?

Outside of work? Not really in the radio or online sense. I mean, I see stuff online like anybody does, people complaining about taxes or roads or whatever, and sometimes it reminds me of work because transportation stuff is everywhere—my uncle used to say everybody’s an expert once there’s a pothole on their street—but I don’t think random posts are aimed at me.

It’s more the work side. Since I got that county safety award, certain people there have been twisting my inspection reports, asking these pointed budget questions, like they’re trying to make me look crooked. My supervisor keeps saying it’s just normal review, but I can tell when something’s coordinated. It feels like they’re trying to discredit me.
Have you ever felt that events or messages in the news, on social media, or in public places were specifically about you or meant for you, even if they didn’t involve people at work?

Not really outside of work, no. I don’t think the news or social media is sending me messages or anything like that.

I’m here because of what’s happening at work. Ever since that county safety award, certain people have been twisting my inspection reports, asking these pointed budget questions like they’re trying to make me look crooked. And my supervisor keeps saying it’s just normal review, but I know what normal review looks like. I’ve been around reports and inspections long enough—my dad used to keep every receipt in a shoebox, so maybe I get the documentation thing from him—but this feels different.

It feels coordinated, like they’re trying to discredit me.

Have you ever felt that random events, like things happening around you or messages in the environment, were specifically about you or had a hidden meaning for you, even when other people didn’t seem to notice anything unusual?

Not random things, no… not like a billboard or some song on the radio has a secret message for me. I don’t really think that way.

What I mean is, at work it’s different. Since that county safety award, people started acting funny around my inspection reports. They’ll bring up budgets or “documentation” in this pointed way, like they’re setting up a record to make me look crooked. My supervisor keeps saying it’s just normal review, but I know what normal looks like. I’ve been doing inspections long enough.

It feels coordinated, like they’re trying to discredit me. I know other people don’t seem to notice it, but they’re not the ones whose name is on the reports.

Have you ever felt that things happening in the world around you, like events in the news or things people say in public, are connected to you or have a special meaning for you personally, even if they don't seem to involve you directly?

Not really the news or people on the street, no. I don’t walk around thinking every headline is about me or anything like that.

It’s more—like I said—it’s what’s happening at work. Ever since I got that county safety award, certain people started going through my inspection reports different, twisting things, asking these budget questions in a way that feels set up. Like they’re trying to make me look crooked.

And my supervisor keeps saying, “That’s just normal review,” but I know the difference. I’ve done this job long enough. My uncle used to say you can tell when somebody’s asking a question to learn something versus asking it to catch you, and that’s what this feels like. Coordinated. Like they’re trying to discredit me.

Have you ever felt that things happening in the world, like events in the news or things people say in public, are connected to you or have a special meaning for you personally, even if they don’t seem to involve you directly?

Not the news, no… I don’t think some story on TV is about me personally or anything like that. It’s really work where it’s happening.

Ever since I got that county safety award, certain people started acting different with my inspection reports. They’ll twist what I wrote or ask these budget questions in this really pointed way, like they’re building something to make me look crooked. And I know my supervisor says it’s just normal review, but I’ve been doing this job long enough to know when something’s off.

It’s like—my shop teacher in high school used to say, “Measure twice because someone will always blame the guy holding the tape,” and that stuck with me. So I pay attention to details. And what I’m seeing now feels coordinated. Like they’re trying to discredit me.
Outside of the situation at work, have you ever felt that people were against you or that things in your environment were set up to target you?

Outside of work? No, not really. I mean, I’m not saying the grocery store clerk is in on anything or that my neighbors are setting things up. It’s not like that.

It’s really been since that county safety award at my job. After that, certain people started twisting my inspection reports, asking these pointed budget questions like they’re trying to make me look crooked. And I know my supervisor keeps saying it’s just normal review, but normal review doesn’t feel like that. I’ve been doing inspections long enough to tell when people are just checking paperwork versus building a case.

So outside of work, no… but at work, yeah, it feels coordinated. Like they’re trying to discredit me.
Have you ever felt that people outside of work, such as strangers or organizations in the community, were acting together in a harmful or threatening way toward you?

No, I don’t think it’s strangers or community organizations or anything like that. I’m not walking around thinking the whole town is after me.

It’s really centered at work. Ever since I got that county safety award, certain people there started acting different—twisting my inspection reports, asking these budget questions in this pointed way, like they’re trying to make me look crooked. And I know my supervisor says it’s just normal review, but I can tell when something’s routine and when people are building something.

It just feels coordinated, like they’re trying to discredit me.

Have you ever felt that messages or events in the broader world, like in the news, public announcements, or other media, were specifically directed at you or had a special meaning for you personally, even when they didn’t seem to involve you directly?

No, I wouldn’t say the news or public announcements are sending me messages or anything like that. I’m not looking at a billboard and thinking it’s about me.

What I’m trying to explain is—it’s at work. Ever since I got that county safety award, certain people started treating my reports differently. They’ll twist what I wrote, or they’ll come at me with these budget questions that sound normal on paper, but the way they ask them… it’s like they’re trying to make me look crooked.

And, you know, my supervisor keeps saying it’s just normal review, but I’ve been doing inspections long enough to know the difference. My old shop teacher used to say if you don’t document every little thing, somebody will use it against you later, and that’s kind of what this feels like. Like there’s a coordinated effort to discredit me.

Have you ever felt that neutral or everyday events, like the way people dress, the things they say in passing, or things you see in your daily life, have a special and direct meaning for you, even if they don’t seem connected to you at first glance?

I don’t think so… I mean, people say things in passing all the time, and half the time it’s just people talking. Like at the gas station the other day someone was complaining about potholes, and I started thinking about how we used to have this whole issue with road maintenance schedules, and my uncle always said nobody fixes anything until somebody important complains—sorry, I’m getting off track.

No, I haven’t really noticed clothes or everyday stuff having some special meaning for me. If something feels pointed, it’s usually because of the context, like who’s saying it and where, not just random things out in daily life.
Have you ever felt that things people say or do in everyday life, like comments in line at the store or something you read, were meant for you or had a hidden meaning that others wouldn’t notice?

Not really in everyday life, no. Like if I’m standing in line at the store and somebody says something, I don’t assume it’s aimed at me. I mean, sometimes people talk loud about city stuff or budgets, and that reminds me of work—because I deal with that kind of thing all the time—but I’m not saying strangers are sending me hidden messages.

What I keep coming back to is work. Since I got that county safety award, certain people there started twisting my inspection reports and asking these pointed budget questions, like they’re trying to make me look crooked. My supervisor says it’s just normal review, but… I can tell when something’s normal and when people are coordinating to discredit me.
Have you ever felt that people were plotting against you or working together to harm you in situations outside of work, even if it wasn’t obvious to others?

Outside of work? No, not really. I mean, people can be petty anywhere—I’ve seen neighbors argue over trash cans like it’s a city council meeting—but I’m not saying there’s some group out there trying to get me.

It’s really the work situation. Ever since that county safety award, certain people started twisting my inspection reports and asking these budget questions in a way that makes it sound like I’m doing something wrong. My supervisor keeps calling it normal review, but I know what normal review looks like. This feels coordinated, like they’re trying to discredit me.
Have you ever felt that things people say or do in everyday situations, like in public places or online, are subtly meant for you or have a hidden meaning that others wouldn’t notice?

I don’t think so. Online especially, I mostly scroll past stuff—people argue about everything, road projects, taxes, whatever, and half the time they don’t even know what they’re talking about. Like there was this whole thread once about lane closures and everybody was blaming inspectors, but that’s just people venting, not necessarily about me.

So… no, I wouldn’t say I notice hidden meanings in public or online. If something feels directed at me, it’s usually because there’s an actual reason, not just some random comment or post.
Have you ever felt that neutral or passing comments, like something someone said in a group or online, were secretly about you or had a hidden meaning that others wouldn’t notice?

Not like random comments, no. If somebody in a group says something vague, I don’t automatically think, “Oh, that’s about me.” People talk just to hear themselves talk half the time, especially online.

But at work it’s different. That’s why I’m here. Ever since I got that county safety award, certain people started picking apart my inspection reports in this weird way and asking these budget questions that are… not normal questions. They make it sound like I’m doing something shady, like they’re setting up a story that I’m crooked. My supervisor keeps saying it’s just regular review, but I’ve been there, I know how reviews go. This feels coordinated, like they’re trying to discredit me.

Do you feel that the reason people are targeting you at work is because of your role, your achievements, or who you are in particular—like they’re trying to bring you down because of something significant you’ve done?

Yeah, I think it started after the safety award. Before that, I mean, people at work had opinions, sure—every department has that—but it wasn’t like this.

After the county recognized me, suddenly my inspection reports were getting twisted around, like they were looking for ways to make them sound wrong. And then these budget questions started coming up, really pointed ones, not normal “check the numbers” stuff. More like they were trying to make me look crooked.

My supervisor keeps saying it’s just regular review, but I know what regular review looks like. I’ve been doing this work. It feels coordinated, like certain people don’t like that I got noticed and now they’re trying to knock me down or discredit me.

Do you ever feel that people are targeting you or plotting against you because of who you are or something special about you, like you have a particular importance or role that others are trying to undermine?

Yeah, I mean… I wouldn’t say I’m “special” like that, not in some big way. But I did get that county safety award, and after that it changed. People notice that kind of thing. At work, everybody acts like they’re above jealousy, but then they’ll sit around picking apart someone else’s work while they’re eating lunch out of a microwave container, you know?

But yes, that’s why I’m here. Since that award, certain people have been twisting my inspection reports, asking these really pointed budget questions like they’re trying to make it look like I’m crooked. My supervisor keeps saying it’s normal review, but I know what normal review looks like. This feels coordinated, like they’re trying to discredit me because I got recognized.
